details:
The new nameplates and social UI look more modern, but I feel visibility has taken a step back and could use some reconsideration.

1. Hard to distinguish friends from non-friends:

Previously, a friend's name text itself was displayed in yellow.

Now, only the border/outline is yellow.

However, the border takes up very little visual space, making it noticeably harder to tell at a glance whether someone is a friend.

2. Social panel feels harder to parse:

Previously, the UI reflected a clear information hierarchy — name in yellow, status in smaller white text.

Now everything is roughly the same size and color (white), which makes it take longer to figure out who's doing what.

The banner display eating up space likely contributes to this as well.

3. No way to distinguish Android from PC users: 

I may be mistaken, but the icon that used to appear on Android users' nameplates seems to be missing entirely in the new UI.

This felt like an essential indicator for being considerate toward friends — why was it removed?

I'm sure other users have raised similar points, but as it stands, the current UI seems to prioritize "modern looks" over practicality.

Beyond just needing time to adjust, there are still significant usability issues that need to be addressed.
title: Visibility concerns with the new nameplate/social UI
